d0bf6cb88a.a: Drew brought a proprietary dual unidirectional bezel system that sets the brand apart from the increasingly crowded watch market. He conceived of a design featuring two rotating bezels that operate together, which he had not seen done that way before in existing watches.

a3084af57d.q: Why did Drew decide to start Mount West Watch Co. instead of licensing his bezel design?
a3084af57d.a: Drew initially thought about licensing the bezel to someone else as probably an easier path to success. However, after doing research, he found the process overwhelming and daunting without industry experience. He realized that protecting the invention would cost tens of thousands of dollars anyway, so starting his own company made sense to maintain creative control over the complete watch design.

4825342247.q: What is the angular case design philosophy behind Mount West Watch's Summit collection?
4825342247.a: Drew designed the Summit case with a flat edge rail on the back where most watches continue the circle. He cut that section to create an overhang to prevent the watch from catching on pants while providing maximum traction. He pushed the angular case design further, which eventually resembled a mountain and canyon shape reflecting Utah's jagged landscapes.

7b07d54fb5.q: How did Drew approach the challenge of bringing an innovative bezel concept to market as an independent brand founder?
7b07d54fb5.a: Drew emphasized that nothing moves quickly in watch manufacturing—it is not a three-month process from idea to ready product. The initial starting point was to make a case to fit the proprietary bezel design, which then necessitated making end links, a bracelet, and ensuring aesthetic uniqueness. He wanted to build something completely unique rather than compromise the vision.
